claims.reason: This is a variable from the PosRoots section that the theorem takes as an argument (it is instance-implicit and P is an argument). Nothing in the statement mentions it, so the statement elaborates without it. Mathlib's `instFlipIsReduced [P.IsReduced] [IsTorsionFree R N] : P.flip.IsReduced` (Reduced.lean:202) needs Finite ι, CharZero R, IsDomain R and IsTorsionFree R M from its section variables; the theorem has the first three. Both torsion-freeness facts follow from the other hypotheses. `RootPairing` has the instance `isPerfPair_toLinearMap`, so `P.toLinearMap : M → (N →ₗ[R] R)` and its flip are injective (`IsPerfPair.bijective_left`/`bijective_right`). R is torsion-free over itself because it is a domain. Linear maps into a torsion-free module are torsion-free (LinearMap/Basic.lean:105). `Function.Injective.moduleIsTorsionFree` (Torsion/Free.lean:54), with `map_smul`, then gives `IsTorsionFree R M` and `IsTorsionFree R N`. So `P.flip.IsReduced` can be rebuilt with `have`, and the existing proof then runs unchanged. This only works while `[P.IsReduced]` is kept.

Symmetric to the first entry. `RootPairing.flip_flip : P.flip.flip = P` holds by `rfl` (Defs.lean:139). So `instFlipIsReduced` applied to `P.flip`, using `[P.flip.IsReduced]`, Finite ι, CharZero R, IsDomain R and torsion-freeness of N and M, gives `P.flip.flip.IsReduced`, which is definitionally `P.IsReduced`. The torsion-freeness comes from the perfect pairing over the domain R, as in the first entry. P.IsReduced does not appear in the statement, so deleting it is a pure deletion, and the proof adds one `have` and is otherwise unchanged. The two hypotheses cannot both be deleted, since each is recovered from the other.
